title: Best phone numbers for AI browser agents that read SMS
summary: A browser agent that signs up for a service needs a phone number it controls and a way to read the code that arrives. These are seven providers you can use for that, with prices and the limits each one documents.
body_markdown:
Your browser agent is partway through a signup when the site asks for the code it just texted. It needs a phone number that can receive that text, and a way to read it. Here are seven providers that give you both.


For a browser agent, our pick is Notte: it is the only one here that also runs the browser, so the identity that fills the signup form is the one the code arrives on. If you would rather build on a carrier API, Plivo is cheapest at low volume and Telnyx past about 160 codes a month. One caveat applies to all seven: no provider can make a site send a code, and some sites refuse VoIP numbers.


We make Notte, so our entry is marked "(ours)". Prices and quotes come from each provider's own pages, read on November 11, 2026. We did not run a test for this post.


## How we picked


We fixed five criteria before reading a single pricing page:


- How the code reaches your agent: a webhook, polling, or a function it can wait on.
- What the provider says about number types and about codes sent by other companies' sites.
- Cost: monthly number rent plus the price of each incoming text.
- What can block you on day one: registration, trial limits, plan requirements.
- Agent tooling: an MCP server, CLI or SDK call that does the work, not one that only searches the docs.


We group the providers by how much you build yourself. Carrier APIs (Plivo, Telnyx, Twilio) come first: they forward each incoming text to your server, and you write the code that reads it. Services built for agents (AgentCall, AgentPhone, Inkbox, Notte) follow: they give your agent a call that reads the texts. Each group is alphabetical, so nobody ranks first by default. Prices are US list prices before tax, and carrier fees are extra where noted. For the browser the agent runs in, see[the browser automation stack in 2026](https://www.notte.cc/blog/browser-agent-stack-2026) .


## Why the code does not always arrive


A number can receive texts and still not receive the one you need. Services check the line type behind a number, and some refuse the ones that look like VoIP. Twilio's[guide to filtering VoIP numbers before sending a one-time code](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/filter-voip-before-otp-verification) , a 2022 post, says a non-fixed VoIP number "is often what you get with Google Voice or Twilio", and that VoIP numbers "are often correlated with bots".[Telnyx writes](https://telnyx.com/resources/google-voice-verification) that "Google and other platforms may block VoIP numbers from receiving SMS codes" and that carrier-grade numbers keep "higher eligibility". That improves the odds but does not guarantee a code.


Bandwidth gives the most detail. Its[support page](https://www.bandwidth.com/support/en/articles/12823146-why-did-i-not-receive-a-2fa-message-on-my-bandwidth-number) lists nine brands that do not send 2FA to its numbers (Google, Meta, Outlook, Twitter, Venmo, Wells Fargo, Tinder, Zelle and Ameriprise), says the list is not complete, and offers no workaround. Twilio also redacts one-time passcodes in inbound messages on trial accounts and marks them failed, as[error 30038](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/30038) describes, and its fix is to upgrade.


Registration is a separate issue. Twilio, Telnyx and Plivo document brand and campaign registration (10DLC) and toll-free verification as requirements for sending. For the seven providers below, we did not find a page that says whether receiving on an unregistered number is allowed, so ask before you build around it.


## The options


### 1. Plivo


Plivo sells phone numbers and SMS and voice APIs to developers, and its[CLI is documented for agents](https://www.plivo.com/docs/cli/agents) . Inbound texts are posted to the[Message URL](https://www.plivo.com/docs/messaging/use-cases/receive-sms/receive-sms) of your application, with` From` ,` To` and` Text` in the body.


- Best for: the lowest number rent of the three carriers, and a CLI an agent can drive.
- Catch: the CLI has no headless login, so a person runs` plivo login` once on the agent's machine, and Plivo's pages do not say whether receiving needs US registration.
- Pricing:[local number $0.50 a month, toll-free $1.00](https://www.plivo.com/phone-numbers/pricing/us/) ;[$0.0077 per SMS](https://www.plivo.com/sms/pricing/us/) on long code, inbound and outbound, plus carrier surcharges.


The CLI returns JSON with` -o json` , previews changes with` --dry-run` and asks for` --yes` before it spends.


### 2. Telnyx


Telnyx sells carrier-grade phone numbers and messaging through an API, and describes itself as a licensed provider. Inbound texts arrive as a` message.received` webhook, and its[local MCP server](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/development/mcp/local-mcp) can search for and buy numbers and send messages.


- Best for: the lowest published inbound rate of the seven, and an MCP server that can buy the number for you.
- Catch: the MCP server lists no tool for reading inbound messages, so you still run a webhook receiver, and Telnyx's own article says some platforms block VoIP numbers.
- Pricing:[numbers from $1 a month](https://telnyx.com/pricing/numbers) plus $0.10 a month to add SMS;[local SMS $0.004 per message part](https://telnyx.com/pricing/messaging) inbound and outbound, plus a carrier fee.


### 3. Twilio


Twilio sells phone numbers and messaging APIs. Numbers come through the[Phone Numbers API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/phone-numbers/api) and inbound texts go to your webhook.


- Best for: teams that already run Twilio and want the number on the same account.
- Catch: its MCP server is a public beta that only searches docs ("It does not execute API calls on your behalf"), and trial accounts have inbound one-time passcodes redacted.
- Pricing:[local number $1.15 a month, toll-free $2.15](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/sms/pricing/us) ; $0.0083 per segment inbound and outbound, plus carrier fees, "current as of October 2026".


### 4. AgentCall


AgentCall sells US and Canada phone numbers to AI agents, and says what the feature is for: tests of flows you control. An API provisions the number and returns the code from a single` waitForOTP()` call, or sends it to your webhook with the full message, according to its[product page](https://agentcall.co/product) .


- Best for: end-to-end tests of SMS verification flows in apps you control.
- Catch: live code extraction needs the Pro plan on new accounts, coverage is the US and Canada, and the page frames the feature for "apps you control", not third-party signups.
- Pricing:[Pro is $19.99 a month plus usage](https://agentcall.co/product) ; numbers from $2 a month, $0.008 per message received and $0.015 per message sent; the 72-hour trial needs a card and allows five send attempts.


### 5. AgentPhone


AgentPhone sells prepaid phone numbers to AI agents. Its MCP server can read message history, so an agent can check for a code without running a webhook. The[MCP guide](https://docs.agentphone.ai/mcp.md) shows` get_messages` for that, and notes that a text arriving does not wake the assistant, so it recommends a webhook for real-time handling.


- Best for: a small prepaid setup, with $5 of free credit and no card.
- Catch: the usage page does not say what type of number you get, and lists only US and Canada standard numbers, with UK numbers on enabled accounts.
- Pricing:[US and Canada numbers $3.00 every 30 days](https://docs.agentphone.ai/usage.md) ; SMS $0.02 per segment inbound and outbound.


### 6. Inkbox


Inkbox gives AI agents identities with a dedicated phone number they can send and receive texts on. An agent reads texts with` identity.list_texts(is_read=False)` or receives them by webhook, as the[phone docs](https://inkbox.ai/docs/capabilities/phone.md) describe.


- Best for: a dedicated number your agent texts from and reads by API.
- Catch: its pricing page calls the number VoIP ("1 dedicated VoIP phone number"), the type the sources above say some services filter.
- Pricing:[the Developer plan is $25 a month](https://inkbox.ai/pricing) with one number and 300 SMS/MMS a month in the US and Canada; extra messages are $0.03, or $0.02 on your own 10DLC campaign.


### 7. Notte (ours)


We build cloud browsers and agents, and a persona is the identity an agent uses to sign up and log in. A[persona](https://docs.notte.cc/concepts/personas) holds an inbox, a credential vault and a phone number. Our docs say the persona system "integrates with both the browser session and the secure vault", so a session that reaches a signup form uses the persona's details and phone number, and nobody has to forward the code.


Outside a session,[persona.wait_for_sms(only_unread=True, timeout=120)](https://docs.notte.cc/sdk-reference/nottepersona/wait_for_sms.md) polls the persona's inbox until a message arrives, with defaults of a 60 second timeout and a 5 second poll interval. The same messages are at[GET /personas/{persona_id}/sms](https://docs.notte.cc/api-reference/personas/persona-sms-list) .


- Best for: browser agents. The number lives on the same identity as the agent's inbox and vault, and that identity is attached to the browser session, so the agent reads the code from the identity that filled the form.
- Catch: our docs do not state the number's type or the countries available, and listing SMS marks the messages as read, so a second` only_unread` read will not see them.
- Pricing:[personas are available on every plan](https://www.notte.cc/pricing) , capped at 5 on Free, 50 on Developer and 200 on Startup, and the docs say each persona "incurs additional charges for the email and phone services". The amounts are not published. To get phone numbers on your personas, write tohello@notte.cc .


Our[agent identities post](https://www.notte.cc/blog/agent-identities) and the[personas walkthrough](https://www.notte.cc/blog/from-zero-to-authenticated-building-self-sufficient-ai-agents-with-notte-personas) cover what a persona is.


## The numbers side by side

Plivo Pay as you go $1.27 + carrier surcharge CLI needs a one-time human login


Telnyx Pay as you go $1.50 + carrier fee MCP cannot read inbound texts


Twilio Pay as you go $1.98 + carrier fees MCP is docs-only, trial redacts codes

Inkbox Plan $25.00 Number stated as VoIP

Prices and limits checked on November 11, 2026 against each provider's docs and pricing pages. US list prices, one message part per code. AgentCall's figure is the Pro plan ($19.99), one number at "from $2" and 100 received messages. Inkbox's plan covers 300 texts. AgentPhone's is one number for 30 days plus 100 incoming segments. Carrier fees are extra for Plivo, Telnyx and Twilio.


Here is what 100 codes a month cost:


Plivo is the cheapest of the three carriers at 100 codes a month. Telnyx's lower inbound rate wins past about 160 codes: at 1,000 codes a month it is Telnyx $5.10, Plivo $8.20 and Twilio $9.45, before carrier fees.


## Who we left out


Sinch ended sales of its standalone SMS API on April 15, 2026 and[points new work to its Conversation API](https://developers.sinch.com/docs/sms) . Azure Communication Services[does not let you buy a phone number with free credits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/communication-services/concepts/numbers/phone-number-management-for-united-states) . We could not read Vonage's price pages, so we make no claims about it. Bandwidth is worth a visit for the 2FA page quoted above. SignalWire, Bird, Infobip and AWS End User Messaging we read and left out to keep the list comparable. Bird and Infobip both document MCP servers and are the first two we would add in an update.


Voice agent platforms such as Vapi, Retell, Bland and ElevenLabs hand out numbers for calls, and the texting they support is secondary. iMessage-first APIs such as Linq and Sendblue are built for texting people. Verification APIs such as Twilio Verify, Prelude and Telesign send codes to your users, which is the opposite job.


Services that rent a number per activation, such as SMSPool, 5sim, TextVerified, VirtualSMS and SV Number, are the other obvious answer, and we left them out. They exist to receive codes from other companies' sites. SV Number's own page says "Acceptance depends on that service", and DaisySMS[closed on March 26, 2026](https://daisysms.com/) . WhatsApp's[terms of service](https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service) bar creating accounts "through unauthorized or automated means", and Google's[terms of service](https://policies.google.com/terms) bar "bypassing our systems or protective measures". A list for agents that act on accounts their owners control should not lead with them.


## How to choose


- If your agent runs in a browser, start with Notte. The persona, with its inbox, vault and phone number, is attached to the browser session, so the agent that fills the form also reads the code.
- If the codes come from apps you run, go by price and by what you already use: Plivo is cheapest at 100 codes a month, Telnyx once you pass about 160, and Twilio if you already have an account.
- If you want less to build and no browser, pick AgentCall for testing your own flows.
- If you need numbers outside the US and Canada, the services built for agents here cover the US and Canada, AgentPhone adds UK numbers on enabled accounts, and Notte publishes no list. Twilio lists numbers in[100+ countries](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/phone-numbers) and Telnyx in[130+](https://telnyx.com/products/phone-numbers) .
- If a site refuses the number, no provider here fixes that. Try your target site with the number before you build around it, and read Bandwidth's 2FA page first.
